title: A trace that ends at the next act: the sign comes back, but it is never read
setup: Experiment 38c · 38b's slow trace (3% a moment), wiped when the next act begins, Olvasó's or the habit's · same runs and seeds · 5 lives each
question: If the lasting trace ends at the next act, does it belong to its act again, and can a word then read it?

points: After the habit's acts the hand is now almost always quiet and read as quiet (0.1-3.5%), after Olvasó's own the trace is still felt and left unread (77-80%). Who acted is told from the reading at 0.49-0.57 (0.58-0.67 with words formed), against 0.28-0.34 for the short trace and about 0 for the longer one. Both controls are at chance.
The flood is gone: 113-117 intentions a day (264-266 for the longer trace), the habit's share back to 17-18%, gaming's harm 8.7 a day (19.3), the inside view back to 0.25-0.28.

But no word ever read the ending trace while it was strong, in any life (0.0%, against 8-11% for the longer trace with words): acts come every few moments, so a trace wiped at the next act is short again.
note: Ending the trace at the next act restores authorship and does nothing for reading. The doer is still told by a hole (felt and unread against quiet), not by a word that reads 'I did this'. In this toy world a trace can belong to one act or be read, not both.
